correctness.rationale: The source formula is reconstructed over an explicit \(\mathbb F_8\) model. The trace-zero set has \(36\) points, the resulting code has length \(37\) and rank \(7\), and the complete \(128\)-word census exactly reproduces the published ordinary enumerator. Every binary message subspace is generated once in RREF; the dimension counts agree with Gaussian binomial coefficients. For each basis, the bitwise union of the basis-codeword supports is exactly the support of the generated subcode. Thus the \(29211\)-subspace census is exhaustive and proves every support multiplicity and minimum in the claim.

value.rationale: The primary paper highlights the m=3 member for its excellent best-known distance parameters and gives a detailed few-weight enumerator, making its higher-support geometry a natural next invariant. The complete SSWD is strictly finer than both the ordinary weight distribution and the generalized-weight hierarchy: it determines every support layer for all 29211 nonzero-dimensional subcodes and exact minimizer multiplicities. This is a compact, reproducible higher-support fingerprint of a newly published highlighted code rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
